floor_history.headline: recon: honest floor 48 -> 47 (xor operand order); residual attributed to sched1 block-5 multiply order (~38), un-coalesced dist copy into $a0 (~5, sibling func_8002D518's closed residual), and reorg s
Structural: honest floor 47 -> 10/202 — named cross-product locals per side test (-24), centroid term first in the XOR with the locals reused across tests (-9), sibling LZCS clobber footprint $12-$15
Floor 10 -> 7/202: the tail residual is CLOSED by an if/return-0 block-structure change, which unlocked the s2-banked LZCR slot operand; residual A is now an allocation question, not a schedule.

First faithful permuter workspace for func_8002D780 built and validated; 55,531-iteration campaign found nothing — its metric is anti-correlated with the engine's on this chassis — and nine embedded-a
Floor 7 -> 2/202: residual B closed (the dist copy survives cse only when the carrier is multiply-defined AND declared before lzcr) and the LZCR slot-address order closed by splitting the LZCS island

Residual A fully attributed from the dumps: it is one local-alloc qty_compare_1 TIE (dz and dx both 3 refs / 7 insns in the target's emission order), not a scheduling wall; 37 variants in four batches

Solver typed both halves of the last 2 insns: sched is solvable (180/720 statement orders reach the target's emission order) but on that order local-alloc sees dz and dx tied on every qty_compare_1 in

frontier.hypothesis: The original compile presented local-alloc with an extra reference, quantity or copy in block 7 that the final 202 instructions do not show, and the surviving-copy route is the one still open.
frontier.mechanism: Only reload/flow2 delete_noop_moves, reorg's delay-slot steal and jump2 cross-jumping remove instructions after local_alloc. The delay-slot route is already spoken for (the ax subu fills the test-2 bltz slot), so the no-op-move route is the candidate: a copy that survives to local-alloc merges its qty with dx's via combine_regs (n_refs 3 -> 5, clear of dz) and then vanishes when both pseudos land in the same hard register.
frontier.next_probe: s7 measured the blocker exactly -- cse folds every SINGLE-DEF copy. Give the copy carrier a second definition the way s5's `m` carrier gets one: hoist the test-3 difference computation so the carrier is assigned in the enclosing test-2 arm and re-assigned inside the test-3 block, then read tmp/grind/func_8002D780/dumps/code6cac_b.cse and .lreg to confirm the copy insn survives into local-alloc BEFORE scoring anything. Keep build_insns at 202.

frontier.hypothesis: The extra_qty vector ('one more temp: refs=2 span=[2,4) pri=10000') flips the seats without touching dz's or dx's own comparator columns.
frontier.mechanism: It is the only 1-atom vector in the inverse.py report that leaves both tied quantities untouched: an additional short-lived quantity born at the top of block 7 changes what find_free_reg has already handed out by the time the tied pair is reached, so dz can be pushed off $v1 without changing its priority.
frontier.next_probe: Spell a seventh test-3 local whose value is genuinely consumed (not a dead store) and is born at the top of the block -- the obvious candidate is splitting one of the four multiply operands into a named intermediate -- measured against the h1 statement order, with build_insns checked to stay at 202. Not spelled in s7.

frontier.hypothesis: A decomp-permuter campaign on the 2-floor chassis finds the last two instructions where the s4 campaign on the 7-floor chassis found nothing.
frontier.mechanism: s7 has typed the residual as a local-alloc tie whose only remaining C-side inputs are an extra quantity or a surviving copy -- exactly the temporary-introduction and statement-reordering moves in the permuter's pass set, and the s4 campaign's neighbourhood was dominated by residuals B and C, which are now closed.
frontier.next_probe: Regenerate base.c from memory/grind/func_8002D780/candidate.c into the validated workspace tmp/grind/func_8002D780/s4/nonmatchings/func_8002D780 (four hurdles + rebuild recipe in evidence.md [s4]), launch with tools/permuter_campaign.py, wait IN-TURN with `permuter_campaign.py wait --dir <ws>`, harvest with --stop before the turn ends, and re-score every find on the engine sandbox (the s4 finding that the permuter's weighted metric is anti-correlated with the engine's here still applies). The family classification of the body -- the FAKE `m` re-store plus the six difference locals -- is still unsettled and must be recorded before any candidate-ready submission.
